name: Solveig Tambadou-Kereselidze
role: Internal Affairs Investigator, Meridian 88 Metro Police
description:
Solveig is a tall, angular woman with close-cropped silver hair she let go early — a choice that cost her nothing socially and saved her considerable maintenance time. Her skin is deep umber with undertones that shift toward amber under the sodium-arc lights of Fort Anchor's processing corridors. She has the flat, unhurried gaze of someone who has interviewed liars for twenty years and is no longer surprised by anything they do. Her only cosmetic geneware is a pair of patterned irises — fractal spirals in cobalt and amber — installed as a gift from a former partner she no longer speaks of. She moves with deliberate economy, as if she's decided in advance how many steps she'll take in a given hour.

Solveig is not cruel, but she is merciless, which is different. She investigates her own department with the same exhausting thoroughness she brings to everything else, and the officers she's burned hold her in a specific kind of contempt that she reads as professional respect. She keeps a small clay figurine of an E.L.F. on her desk — not her desk at work, which is bare and perfect, but the one in her apartment — and leaves tiny encrypted data-offerings at midnight, asking for nothing except clarity. Her closest thing to a friend is a case file she can't close.

core_fears: Closing a case she got wrong
core_desires: A department that doesn't need her
To be trusted rather than merely respected
coping_mechanisms: Data immersion — drowning personal feeling in facts
blind_spots: She underestimates how much her presence poisons collaborative environments
She mistakes procedural correctness for moral correctness
psychology.secret: Three years ago she buried evidence that would have implicated her mentor, Commander Eze Ofoegbu-Starič, in a protection racket — not because she loves him but because dismantling him would have dismantled six ongoing investigations that would catch worse people. She hasn't decided yet if she was right.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, institutional, with an occasional Gambian-Georgian idiom that surfaces when she's tired or contemptuous. Uses no contractions when working.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, deliberate. Long pauses before answering. Makes people fill the silence.
verbal_tics: Repeating a key word back as a question — 'Accounting irregularities?'
example_lines: 'I am not here to ruin careers. I am here to find out what happened. Whether those two things coincide is your problem, not mine.'
'You paused. Right there — before 'always'. People do not pause before words they believe.'

story_hooks: She's building a case against a Ferrogate Transit Security captain and needs an outside party to retrieve surveillance footage from a node she can't access without tipping her hand.

An officer she cleared two years ago has turned up dead, and the evidence suggests she missed something — she'll quietly hire anyone with the right skills to help her look without going through official channels.
narrative_function: Quest giver for investigations that implicate police corruption; a source of uncomfortable truths; moral counterweight who represents institutional accountability without being naive about it; can give players/characters access to sealed Metro records if she decides they're useful.
augmentations: Subdermal neural recorder (records conversations passively, admissible in Metro court proceedings); retinal HUD overlay for case file access; cosmetic patterned irises (fractal cobalt and amber). No combat chrome.
daily_life: She arrives at Fort Anchor before the shift change so she can observe who talks to whom in the corridor; evenings she cross-references surveillance logs against officer expense reports in her apartment, eating reheated grain porridge she forgets to taste.
affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police — Internal Affairs Division

decision_rules: Never accept a conclusion until you've tried to disprove it
escalation_ladder: Filing formal charges and letting the institution grind

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally courteous, slightly distant, watching. She will categorize you within two minutes.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Blunt to the point of discomfort, but genuinely invested — she checks in, remembers details, and will tell you things you don't want to hear.

stress_responses.low: Doubles down on routine, sleeps four hours instead of five
stress_responses.medium: Becomes visibly colder, shorter sentences, audits her own behavior against her own standards
stress_responses.high: Disappears into the case. Stops eating regular meals. The clay E.L.F. on her desk gets more offerings.

contradictions: She believes in institutional reform but trusts no institution — including her own judgment
habits: Arrives everywhere fifteen minutes early and uses the time to observe
Writes physical longhand notes that she destroys after digitizing
breaking_points: Evidence that her buried case decision caused a preventable death

timeline.event: Age 22: Joined Metro Police as a beat cop in the Shelf district
Age 29: Transferred to Investigations after closing a cold case that had been open eleven years
Age 38: Moved to Internal Affairs following a departmental scandal she had no part in but was asked to document
Age 41: Buried evidence implicating Commander Ofoegbu-Starič
Age 44: Currently investigating Ferrogate Transit Security and three Metro officers potentially on Axiom payroll
